correctness.rationale: Unrestricted proof: a prime divisor sum forces a prime-power input with prime exponent-plus-one. Primality of \(\sigma(\varphi(n))\) forces a power-of-two totient and distinct Fermat odd factors. Binary digit counts exclude odd composites; parity and exponent parity exclude multiples of four. Fermat index zero forces \(n=6\), which fails; two-prime support then gives \(n=2F_j\), and mod 3, mod 8, and factoring \(3^{2h}-1\) uniquely force \(n=10\). Prime inputs are treated exactly without assuming finite Fermat-prime classification. Exact computational replay corroborates the result.
